To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the bias correction technique is effective in improving forecast performance; (b) the ensemble calibration scheme yields further improvements in forecast performance; and (c) both techniques are effective when combined.

We developed an effective technique for bias correction of wind direction forecasts from NWP models, and an ensemble postprocessing method for wind direction forecasts, which are based on a state‐of‐the‐art circular‐circular linear regression and Bayesian model averaging, respectively.

(i) the circular‐circular bias correction method performs well for the wind direction forecasts from the UWME, (ii) the Bayesian model averaging scheme with von Mises densities as component distributions performs better than a standard ensemble mean, and (iii) the combination of these two methods results in the best forecasts.
